text: Global security developments, such as terrorism, epidemics, economic crisis and environmental disaster, impact Singaporeans at home and abroad.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: What role can Singaporeans play in defence and how can we be a resilient society in the face of such varied security challenges?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: The most advanced military hardware in the world would be useless without the willingness of our people to defend the country.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: Our safety and security depend on the contributions of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: Singapore is worth defending and can be defended.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: This core belief must be instilled and maintained in every Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: What we cannot defend, we do not own.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: How is MINDEF engaging Singaporeans to strengthen the commitment in the defence of Singapore?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Thanks to them, Singaporeans have enjoyed decades of relative peace and stability.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: For the younger generations of Singaporeans, events, such as Konfrontasi, racial riots and Singapore's road to Independence, are study subjects rather than personal memories.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: For many in the younger generation, the outpouring of recollections when Mr Lee Kuan Yew passed on, may have been the first time they learned of the hardships our Pioneers had endured to build the Singapore of today.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Even as we move past SG50 and SAF50 celebrations, there are still many ways in which we can recognise our Pioneers and tap on their wealth of experiences.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: How is MINDEF working to engage younger generations of Singaporeans on defence issues and foster a stronger commitment to defence amongst our youths?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Does MINDEF plan to tap on the experiences and wisdom of SAF Pioneers?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: How is MINDEF using social media to engage young people and Singaporeans at large?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Given the multifaceted nature of threats to Singapore's security, all Singaporeans must stand ready to play their part in the Total Defence of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Modern threats evolve quickly and our concept of Total Defence must also be updated to adapt to global, regional and societal developments and challenges.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Can MINDEF provide an update on its 2016 Total Defence Campaign?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides the NSmen, regulars and NSmen, the buy-in extends to their families, friends, colleagues and society at large.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: ACCORD members have played and are playing a significant part in building public acceptance and support for Singapore's security and defence needs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Can MINDEF provide an update on the work of various ACCORD Councils in the past year?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: How extensive and representative has public engagement been and will be done?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: SAF also has to be understanding, accommodating and compassionate while maintaining the integrity of our defence system where it is the duty of every Singaporean man.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But he only got to know about this one week before the manning period.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As it was a rare opportunity for him, he would like to extend his trip for another 11 days on a personal holiday.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, the human resources department of his company, which is a major local bank, emailed to the SAF to appeal for him.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I have not received his payslip and commission.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I have also not been furnished the total cost of business trip to Italy.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I have to finally state categorically that I manage 300+ men.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The standards I set have to be complied with by the rest of the men.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I am sure such instances are very rare, but I do hope that MINDEF could advise their officers to be more mindful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As our security environment becomes increasingly complex and volatile, we need not only advanced equipment and technologies, but also the continued contribution and commitment of every NSman.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, I will talk about three areas of efforts important to NSmen – effective training, meaningful recognition and instilling pride.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the process, I should be able to answer most of the questions raised by Members in their cuts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Lee Yi Shyan asked about improvement in our training and learning systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The soldiering skills of our servicemen are gained, honed and maintained through rigorous training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But Singapore does not have large tracts of land for military training and we have to make training realistic through innovative means.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To allow servicemen to gain greater confidence in their shooting skills and handling weapon systems, live-firing ranges are now equipped with targetry systems that can replicate realistic operational scenarios.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Further, live training is augmented by simulation training, which develops our soldiers' cognitive decision-making skills, while sharpening their physical war-fighting skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It hosts a suite of simulators that provide tactical training for selected weapons and platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Besides rigour and realism, another critical element of training is safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about public engagement on training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think this is a very valid concern that we also share.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Instead, we will strive to continue to improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We recognise that for every Singaporean male serving NS, there will be loved ones at home worrying about their safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To give them peace of mind, family members who visit the Basic Military Training Centre (BMTC) are shown how training is conducted and the safety precautions we take.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Training safety is also featured in many of our public engagement events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And I have noted Mr Pritam Singh's suggestions for more of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I hope the Members of this House, especially all those like Dr Lim Wee Kiak, who are still actively serving NS, will help us by playing a part to assure the public and all our residents on our strong emphasis on training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Unfortunately, much as we try, there will inevitably be injuries and casualties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked about our compensation framework, and gave several suggestions, when that happens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Beyond compensation provisions, our welfare frameworks provide additional support to the servicemen and their families through the SAF Benevolent Fund and the SAF Care Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But any form of compensation would never be adequate to make up for any permanent loss of limb, or worse, life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I was trying to catch them, after hearing them for the first time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the impression I get is, I think, do not go down the road where recognition of NS becomes a valuation of the sacrifice and any compensation counts to the dollar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: You lost a limb, you lost a loved one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we will have to do what we can that is fair, and we hope that our compensation and welfare frameworks can provide adequate support when unfortunate incidents happen in the course of service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Pritam Singh also asked about the management of NSmen undergoing Operationally Ready NS (ORNS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let us first talk about when ORNS starts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And I must say that it is also in the interest of the SAF for ORNS to start as soon as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But not in the first year, because those would have just "ORD-ed" or completed their compulsory two-year NS stint, and it is quite difficult for them to be called back in the first year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Currently, the majority of NSmen in operational units are called up for ORNS training within the first two years after their ORD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But some NSmen may begin their ORNS training cycle later for a variety of reasons, such as their being overseas for work or study, deferred due to heavy commitments, academic or professional, or they are pending medical reviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They may also be trainers or headquarter staff who do not have a unit and need to be redeployed to another unit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That accounts for the majority of the reasons why ORNS starts later for certain people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Notwithstanding, where feasible, we will ensure ORNS training starts as soon as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is in our interest because, especially when you ORD as a unit, you want to keep the unit together and the camaraderie going.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One way is to ensure that the first few years of ORNS comprise shorter, low-key trainings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, we have tied up with local universities to facilitate the call-up of the students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This also ensures that ORNS training starts early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, is to make some changes to how we deploy NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, trainers who went through full-time NS at the Basic Military Training Centre (BMTC) may be deployed as training instructors at our Training Institutes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These measures ensure that ORNS training starts early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: More importantly, it holds the unit together, keeping the camaraderie going.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Then, there is the issue of when ORNS ends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A great number were able to complete by their early 30s, when they have many more preoccupations in life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is a structure to the 10 years of ORNS – starting with low-key, perhaps company-level training, before ramping up to high-key, longer exercises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, when an NSman misses a high-key training due to health reasons, extended overseas assignment or, like Mr Baey Yam Keng just told the story, due to being given an incentive trip, he may then disrupt his ORNS cycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some of us may have experienced that ourselves and we end up undergoing more low-key ICTs and not fulfilling our high-key ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are a couple of scenarios when that happens; when you miss high-key ICTs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If he remains in the same unit, then he may be called up for other ORNS activities throughout the year, such as operational briefings, exercise preparations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These are typically low-key ICTs and they clock up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If he is deployed to another unit, he will then follow the operational requirements and call-ups of the new unit, which will include both low- and high-key ICTs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Deferments for various work, health, family reasons, they are ever rising.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are all getting so busy, and the SAF needs to be understanding to these competing life priorities – a point that Mr Baey had just made, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But, at the same time, this disrupts and affects the completion of the ORNS cycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to do our best to facilitate as many NSmen as possible to complete their ORNS cycle early, while meeting the SAF's operational needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about updates on what we 	can do more in terms of recognition for NSmen, and this is one of the key recommendations of CSNS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have been finding ways to show appreciation to our NSmen and those who support them – the NSman Tax Relief, National Service Housing, Medical and Education (NS HOME) Awards, SAFRA facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These forms of recognition are important to let them know that their sacrifices are deeply appreciated and for the greater good of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will enhance the recognition for NSmen in three ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, today, we have the Family Recognition Voucher scheme where NSmen receive vouchers which they can use at many outlets and merchants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will enhance it and rename it as the NS Excellence Award.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the change is not just in name.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The number of NSmen who are awarded vouchers in recognition of their good performance during ICTs and NS courses will increase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, in the later part of 2016, we will enhance the basic life and personal accident insurance coverage for NSmen from SAF, SPF and SCDF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will cover all incidents during full-time NS and  ORNS activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The new SAFRA Punggol club will be completed in April 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Actually, it is kind of completed and is just waiting to be opened.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It has a very attractive set of facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the northeastern region, there are 82,000 NSmen and their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I believe the clubhouse will serve them well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But ultimately, the best reward for NSmen is that, together, all of us, we live in a peaceful Singapore and our families are safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak also asked what more we can do to help NSmen in their professional and personal development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, SAF already deploys some NSFs to vocations where their existing skills can contribute to operational requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These include NSFs with relevant medical or engineering backgrounds, who can serve as medics or technicians or navy medical officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In addition, we will continue to work with the Workforce Development Agency (WDA) to accredit the leadership and vocational skills learnt during NS, such as for military police, paramedics, and aircraft technicians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will do more to consider the skills and abilities of our servicemen during deployment, while balancing operational requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, the manning of critical vocations and commander positions must always remain a priority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ironically, these are the key positions where you do not receive skills certificates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In NS, the commanders always say, "In NS, we chiong sua".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It means we charge up the hills together, build camaraderie, train together, and that is something we take back and is valuable to us, but there is no certificate for that.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But each of us understands, that when we went through that, we took back something and we grew from "boys to men".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We must also recognise stakeholders that support NS, something that Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef raised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Last year, we revamped the Total Defence Awards and recognised 122 NS Advocates who have demonstrated tremendous support for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Digistore Solutions Pte Ltd is an SME that has provided strong support for their NSmen employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In addition to ensuring that their employees' work responsibilities are covered, they provide paid family trips to nearby locations, such as Malacca, Bintan, for employees who complete their ICTs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I heard that during ICTs, they even deploy company transport to send their employees' kids to school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This scheme recognises organisations supportive of NS and Total Defence and encourages more employers and businesses to adopt human resource practices that support our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The NS institution is only as strong as the commitment and fighting spirit of our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We see this spirit in many of our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Despite having to juggle NS duties with day-to-day family and job commitments, these NSmen set aside time to attend courses to upgrade their vocational and leadership skills in preparation for their higher appointments in NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We also see NSmen extending service to contribute to national defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Often, what motivates our NSmen to serve with such dedication are the camaraderie and friendships forged with their fellow NSmen in the units.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Last year, one of our NS Commanding Officers, Lieutenant Colonel (NS) Darren Tan, shared a Facebook note dedicated to his battalion, 823 Singapore Infantry Regiment (SIR).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I assume it was with his wife's approval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First Sergeant (NS) Mok Shing Chi, despite being diagnosed with cancer, continued to serve his ICT with the help and support of his NS buddies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our NSmen can keep this spirit of serving going because Singaporeans are united in supporting NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Volunteers who have completed the requisite training have since been deployed in vocations, such as Auxiliary Security Troopers and Naval Bridge Watch Keepers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Alexander Voss, a Singapore PR and one of our Volunteer Auxiliary Security Troopers, shared, "I have had a growing desire to give back to Singapore, which I think of as my home, and play a part in our nation's defence".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Moving forward, we will continue to see SAFVC volunteers deployed in diverse roles to better support our NSmen in defending Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The introduction of NS is a significant milestone in our nation-building journey, occurring shortly after Singapore gained Independence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Then, in this House, there were heated debates by an earlier generation of Members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, I think the situation is totally different.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are all united in upholding the institution of NS and, as Dr Lim Wee Kiak said, NS has even become a form of national identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Indeed, the efforts of our NSmen and those who support them have been instrumental in establishing the bedrock of peace and stability upon which we have built Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let us continue to ensure NS will remain a source of pride and strength for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But some may wonder: will we make it to SG100?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are confident that our home and way of life are safeguarded by an advanced and highly trained SAF, but we must know that our security agencies cannot do the job on their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ultimately, it is the responsibility of every individual to participate in the defence of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am heartened that many Singaporeans I spoke to during focus group discussions shared this view.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This idea of strength in unity is captured in this year's Total Defence campaign theme "Together We Keep Singapore Strong".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The threats and challenges we face since Total Defence was introduced 32 years ago have evolved, but the message to respond as one people remains equally, if not more, important today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Take the experience of Paris last year, when terrorist attacks claimed 120 victims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The initial shock gave way to a strong show of solidarity by the French.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just two weeks later, Paris hosted the 2015 United Nations Conference on Climate Change involving more than 140 world leaders and around 40,000 attendees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, despite increased public security measures, Parisians have not withdrawn into fear and doubt but have returned to their daily routines in celebration of the city's strength and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As President Hollande said, "  have a cult of death, but we have a love of life." As Mr Amrin Amin pointed out, we need to be resilient as we face evolving threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2011, following the arrest of 15 members of the Singapore JI branch, interracial confidence circles in schools and workplaces were formed to promote inter-religious understanding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We emerged stronger from the episode, but it became clear that security agencies cannot fight the threats alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As members of the public, we can play our part by being vigilant and sounding the alarm if we find something amiss.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The battle today, and in the future, is not one waged by tanks and planes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is a battle that needs to be won in our hearts and minds as we guard against influences that threaten our social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Apart from Islam, religions, such as Buddhism, Hinduism, Christianity, Judaism and Sikhism, also practise certain dietary restrictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, we do not insist that public eating places cater to any specific religious requirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Rather than encouraging any one religious group to push fully for its own strict requirements, our approach has been to accommodate as far as practicable the needs of devotees of different religions while maintaining the common space and common goals for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, in hawker centres, school canteens and food courts, for example, there are halal and vegetarian food stalls, but there are no specific corners for halal or vegetarian tables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This facilitates social integration, where Singaporeans come together, eat in the same space and interact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is the cornerstone of our multiracial society and Singaporeans accept this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Similarly, there is no strict requirement that all restaurant kitchens must be halal-certified before they are allowed to operate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The SAF operates similarly, just like society at large.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In our camps, where space is available, we make provisions for halal food to be prepared separately from non-halal food, but our soldiers eat together in our dining halls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Where space is limited, vegetarian and halal food are brought in from centralised kitchens instead of being prepared in the cookhouse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In operations, like field camps, we provide combat rations that are halal, and vegetarian options are also made available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The preparation of halal food requires strict adherence to the religious stipulations governing the food source, preparation and even storage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For Navy ships, space is always a premium which needs to be maximised and prioritised for key operational requirements, such as for combat systems, ammunitions and equipment spares.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Nonetheless, we make provisions for our Muslim servicemen on board ships by providing options, such as seafood, chicken and vegetables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Similarly, we make provisions for non-Muslim Navy servicemen with specific dietary restrictions, wherever possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our practice is similar to other Navies, including France and the US.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our servicemen and women understand and accept this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They are prepared to make sacrifices where needed and are committed to defending Singapore and all that we stand for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am heartened that Singaporeans understand the importance of the community's role in the nation's defence and provide useful feedback through ACCORD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The response from our NSmen and their families has been very positive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, through the Educational Institutions (EI) Council, four Post-Secondary Education Institutions piloted fitness programmes to help pre-enlistees get ready and fit for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition, the EI Council reached out to Singaporean and PR students in Foreign System Schools and Privately-Funded Institutions to help them understand the importance of NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The United World College of South East Asia was so enthused that they hosted an NS Information Evening for 430 pre-enlistees and their parents from nine Foreign System Schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, the Employer and Business (E&B) Council piloted a post-ICT letter to employers, to recognise useful skills and attributes of our servicemen which are invaluable in the business world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Absolute Kinetics Consultancy Pte Ltd was one of the winners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They demonstrated their strong support for NS by providing incentives for NSmen who excel in their IPPT and recognising employees who do well during NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: What is most heartening is that these projects were initiated and led by members of the respective councils themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2016, we can look forward to an expanded "We Support YOU in NS" programme and more exciting collaborations with Families for Life to reach the wider community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to encourage more pre-enlistee fitness programmes and engender broader-based support for NS through the "NS Mark" later this year, which recognises supportive employers, businesses and organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Amrin Amin and Mr Lee Yi Shyan asked how MINDEF is encouraging Singaporeans to strengthen commitment to defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The SAF regularly organises events to educate the public on our defence capabilities in a fun and engaging way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, the RSAF will organise an Open House in May this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, we launched the Commitment to Defence (C2D) Ambassadors programme to allow our SAF Pioneers to engage and inspire the younger generation with personal stories of Singapore's early struggles and our accomplishments in the face of adversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our younger generation found the sharing sessions interesting, authentic, and I quote, "not something we can get from the Internet".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, C2D Ambassadors like COL (Ret) Goh Lye Choon would captivate his audience by recounting his experience fighting infiltrators in the jungles of Kota Tinggi during Konfrontasi.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: According to C2D Ambassador MAJ (Ret) Ashim Mochtar, our youths are far from apathetic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They are passionate and understand the need for Singapore to stand up for itself.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin asked about the public's readiness to address a variety of evolving threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MINDEF agrees that the public needs to join the conversation on ensuring our future security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, we integrated this year's Total Defence campaign with the SGfuture citizen engagement initiative, under the theme "A Secure and Resilient Nation".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of the discussion participants, Mr Saravenan said, "It was good to see that we feel strongly about our country and care enough to share." Many have also contributed interesting ideas to bring Total Defence to life, such as by running crisis simulation exercises to demonstrate the importance of Total Defence in overcoming hybrid threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to explore how such ground-up ideas can revitalise community action for Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We held a Total Defence exhibition in February and March this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The exhibition featured individuals like Ms Nur Arfa, who was only 13 years old when she volunteered with "Citizens on Patrol" to spread awareness on crime prevention in her neighbourhood; as well as groups like the Religious Rehabilitation Group that fight religious extremist propaganda.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Lee Beng Kit, an exhibition visitor, said, "It is nice to see people contributing to society in their own ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: After all, Total Defence is about everybody coming together to keep Singapore strong, regardless of race, language and religion." We hope that the exhibition showed that there is much each individual can do to keep Singapore strong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This year, we refreshed the Total Defence song "There's a Part for Everyone".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am sure Members can all remember that song from many, many years ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But the updated version is a lot more hip.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, with updated lyrics and a new upbeat arrangement by home-grown band QuickPick, the familiar medley caught on very quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Even Minister Ng Eng Hen was game enough to sing along to the refreshed song, helping us reach out to half a million people through his Facebook page.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Unfortunately, I do not have time to show the video today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope that all of us will renew our commitment to Total Defence each time this song is sung.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also continue to engage Singaporeans through platforms like the ciNE65 short film competition and N.E.mation! digital animation competition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Those who caught the "Ah Boys to Men" movies said it "shed (light) on the untold story of our unsung heroes".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The future is uncertain, but I am confident that if we see ourselves, first and foremost, as one people and have the resolve to work together to strengthen our military, civil, economic, social and psychological defences, we, as a society, will be resilient enough for any challenge that comes our way.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarifications.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I have two clarifications, both for the Senior Minister of State, regarding the NS Mark and NS Gold Mark.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: What are the specific criteria for the companies to achieve these?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Is it possible for them to consider accumulating that?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: For example, if you serve three or four low-key ICTs, it is equivalent to one high-key ICT.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The number of days, added together, forms a sacrifice as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For the first point on the Statutory Boards, I would say that MINDEF agrees with the Member.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On accumulating low-key ICTs to become high-key ICTs, this is a suggestion that had been raised before.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have looked at it and we will probably continue to look at it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Just as I do some extra push-ups, do one more broad jump, one more shuttle run, it does not equal a 2.4-kilometre run.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, there is a limit to that logic.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: There is CSA and I think MINDEF are looking at cybersecurity issues.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am just wondering what is the coordination between the two, because there will be a lot of joint issues faced by both.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: One looks at, I understand, state-related issues; the other looks at domestic, commercial facilities and so on.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think there is probably a lot of coordination required and lots of the types of threats both tackle will be similar.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Its task remit is to secure, if you like, the cyber environment for the whole-of-Government.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The financial cluster is key; transport, power, and so on and so forth.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For the SAF, we are responsible for cybersecurity of our own military networks to make sure that we can conduct a defence – there are some things that I would not tell you – but we can conduct our defence.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My question is directed to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am just following up on the high-key ICT issue.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: According to the CSNS, one of their recommendations was to implement make-up high-key ICTs.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just get an update from the Senior Minister of State how far SAF has gone into this?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because if I hear the Senior Minister of State correctly, it seems as if there may be difficulties in implementing this recommendation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the process, what we lose is that he is no longer in the unit.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To many NSmen, that actually is quite important because your friends and comrades are all from that unit.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: While we try to implement the make-up high-key ICT, it is also in our interest to cater to young people and their many preoccupations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If they can finish their ORNS by their early 30s, then start to have babies, get their flats and start to work hard and be more focused on their career, I think it is a good thing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is totally in our interest to make sure it ends as early as we can, early 30s if possible.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I do not think that I need the Senior Minister of State to remind me that Singapore is a multiracial and multi-religious society.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: The Minister mentioned that it is due to practical reasons or practical issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: My point is that since this is a practical issue or practical problem that exists, has this practical problem been resolved practically?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe if this practical reason can be resolved, it will further foster the inclusivity of SAF or RSN.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Member is quoting me and I do not know what he is quoting.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If he can show what I actually said in the conference or at the meeting, I am more than happy to accommodate what I said.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But I think there is a larger point.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Mr Faisal Manap says he does not need to be reminded that we are a multiracial, multi-religious society.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But he is only championing in his speech for Muslims.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Senior Minister of State Maliki made it clear that if each of us in this House – Muslims champion Muslims, Christians champion Christians, Buddhists champion Buddhists – we have never pushed for each group to fully push for their rights, for their observances.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But we made it clear that, for the Navy, that space is always a premium.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But there is a larger point in this:  what is the tone of the society, the tone of the SAF?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Because in the SAF, I draw from all Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I have people who do not eat beef.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I have people with religious observances, apart from Muslims.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But the overriding principle must be that the SAF's operational concerns must come first, and individual needs sometimes must subsume under that.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I am certain that there are situations where I cannot please all, accommodate all requirements.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I cannot, hand on heart, assure you that all my mobile kitchens are halal.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And sometimes, if we can, we will offer combat rations which are halal, which are pre-prepared.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But fresh rations sometimes are served in the field.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And I think our overall point is: where we can, we will lean forward as with the rest of the society, but always with the understanding that the SAF's needs and operational concerns must come first.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There may be individual sacrifices that we make, but we deploy based on merit as well as commitment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Because I do know of a group of ladies who are actually considering joining but worry about their physical capabilities, myself included.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe that I have voiced out more national issues, compared to Malay/Muslim issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: And I believe it is my role and responsibility as an elected Member of a minority community in the Group Representation Constituency (GRC) system, it is my responsibility and role to voice out Malay/Muslim issues based on the voices that I gather from the community.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: In many countries, the military is seen as a powerful remote organisation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, in that sense, it is very close to home.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: At the same time, it is respected around the region, it is respected by our contemporaries, I think that is quite an important achievement.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am now into my Reservist on Voluntary Extended Reserve (ROVER) stage.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It is something many of us are proud of.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: With that, Madam, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.05 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.45 pm until 4.05 pm.
